B.Sc Nursing seats are counselled by MCC for some institutions, but most nursing, pharmacy and physiotherapy admissions run through state routes that differ.
Specialising means a postgraduate degree after that.
Science with Biology (PCB) is the usual choice.

If the NEET result does not go your way: allied health degrees (B.Sc Nursing, physiotherapy, pharmacy, medical laboratory or radiography technology), BAMS or BHMS through NEET, or a B.Sc in a life science with a later master's in public health or biotechnology.

For NITs and IIITs the NTA has asked for Physics and Maths plus one of Chemistry, Biology, Biotechnology or a technical vocational subject, with a minimum Class 12 mark or percentile.
B.Tech or BE (4 years): mechanical, civil, electrical, chemical, aerospace and more.

If the JEE rank falls short: state engineering entrance tests, private universities through BITSAT, VITEEE or their own tests, or a 3-year diploma followed by lateral entry into the second year of B.Tech.

B.Tech or BE (4 years) in computer science, AI and data science, or similar.

Science with Maths (PCM) plus Computer Science is the usual choice.

If a computer science seat at a top college is out of reach: BCA then MCA, a B.Sc in computer science or data science, or a diploma with lateral entry into B.Tech. Real projects and certificates count for a lot in this field.

CA Foundation from ICAI: provisional registration is possible after Class 10, and the exam is taken after Class 12.
CA runs alongside: Foundation, Intermediate, Final and practical training.

If CA is not for you: B.Com with CMA, CS or CFA alongside, or BBA and an MBA later. Banking and other exams are open after any graduation.

Commerce stream. Take Maths if your board offers it.
UCEED (IITs and a few others), NID DAT, NIFT entrance, and university tests.
The Council of Architecture rule for Class 12 is Physics and Maths plus one more subject from a list, with 45% aggregate marks.
B.Des (4 years), B.Arch (5 years), BFA (3 to 4 years), or degrees in animation, film and fashion.
Architecture needs Physics and Maths plus one more subject from an approved list.

Any stream works for most design courses. Art or Computer Science can help. For Architecture take Physics and Mathematics plus one more subject from the Council of Architecture list (such as Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, Informatics Practices or a vocational subject).

CUET-UG (Psychology) for central universities.

Clinical psychologists then need an RCI-recognised postgraduate clinical psychology qualification (RCI now lists the M.Clin.Psy and Psy.D, replacing the older M.Phil).
Humanities with Psychology is the most common choice.
If a psychology honours seat is hard to get: a BA in Psychology at any good college, then an MA or M.Sc and approved training if you want to practise as a clinical psychologist.
RCI changed its clinical psychology qualifications from 2024-25. Check the current RCI list before choosing a course.

In May 2025 the Supreme Court made 3 years of practice a condition for the Civil Judge exam. Law-news sites report a change in August 2026, with relief for notifications issued up to 31 March 2027. These are secondary reports. Read the judgment and your state High Court notice.

Policy and planning paths: BA in Political Science, Economics or Geography, then MA or MPP.

United States bachelor's tuition per year: 32000 to 45000 USD. College Board 2025-26 averages: public out-of-state US$31,880, private non-profit US$45,000. Many universities charge more, and some charge less.
United States master's tuition per year: 25000 to 60000 USD. Master's programmes vary a lot. STEM master's often cost more.
United States living cost per year: 15000 to 25000 USD. University cost sheets list about US$20,000 to 25,000 including housing, food and insurance. Big cities cost more.
F-1 students can work in their field after graduation on OPT for 12 months. STEM degrees can add a 24-month STEM OPT extension, so up to 36 months. Staying longer usually needs an H-1B work visa.

US median pay for each career comes from O*NET and the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (shown on the careers above). These are US medians for each job, not a guarantee for new graduates. Doctors trained abroad must also pass US licensing (USMLE) and match into a residency; the odds are low.
Canada bachelor's tuition per year: 18867 to 49802 CAD. Statistics Canada 2025/26: average international undergraduate tuition C$41,746. Ontario averages C$49,802, Newfoundland and Labrador C$18,867.

Canada master's tuition per year: 6964 to 35000 CAD. Statistics Canada 2025/26: average international graduate tuition C$24,028. Newfoundland and Labrador averages C$6,964. Professional master's cost more.
Canada living cost per year: 23448 to 30000 CAD. IRCC asks single applicants to show C$23,448 a year for living costs from 1 September 2026 (C$22,895 before). Real costs depend on the city.

A Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) can last up to 3 years for master's graduates, and for bachelor's programmes of 2 years or more. A language test result is needed. Some programmes are not eligible, so check the programme.
No checked figure yet. Statistics Canada table 37-10-0122-01 has current figures by field. Please check before relying on any number.
United Kingdom bachelor's tuition per year: 20000 to 30000 GBP. UKCISA: international students can expect about £20,000 to £30,000 a year. Medicine and dentistry can be over £50,000.
United Kingdom master's tuition per year: 15000 to 35000 GBP. Master's fees are not capped. Most are one year long.

United Kingdom living cost per year: 14052 to 18348 GBP. Student visa maintenance is £1,171 a month outside London and £1,529 in London, counted for up to 9 months (£10,539 and £13,761). This range is the same monthly rates over 12 months. Real costs are higher in London.
The Graduate Route lets graduates stay and work for 2 years (for applications made by 31 December 2026), 18 months (from 1 January 2027), or 3 years for PhD graduates. No job offer is needed.

The median salary of UK graduates in full-time work 15 months after graduating is £30,000 (HESA, 2023/24). Medicine and dentistry graduates have the highest median, £43,749. International graduates earn less on average.
Australia bachelor's tuition per year: 20000 to 50000 AUD. Typical international tuition for bachelor's degrees. Medicine and some specialist degrees cost more.
Australia master's tuition per year: 25000 to 55000 AUD. Master's programmes by coursework.
Australia living cost per year: 29710 to 35000 AUD. The student visa asks single applicants to show A$29,710 a year for living costs. Sydney and Melbourne cost more.
The Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) usually allows 2 to 3 years of work after a bachelor's or master's degree. You must be 35 or under when you apply. Fees rose from 1 March 2026.

Australian Graduate Outcomes Survey: the national median full-time salary was A$71,000 for undergraduates and A$96,600 for postgraduate coursework graduates in 2023. A secondary source reports A$77,000 for undergraduates in 2025.
Netherlands bachelor's tuition per year: 9000 to 20000 EUR. Average institutional fees for non-EU bachelor's students (Study in NL, 2026). Individual programmes differ.
Netherlands master's tuition per year: 12000 to 30000 EUR. Average institutional fees for non-EU master's students (Study in NL, 2026).
Netherlands living cost per year: 13570 to 18000 EUR. The IND financial requirement is €1,130.77 a month from 1 January 2026, about €13,570 a year. Amsterdam is much costlier.

Graduates of Dutch universities, and of top foreign universities, can apply for a one-year orientation permit (zoekjaar) to look for work, within 3 years of graduating. A skilled migrant permit then needs an employer and a minimum salary.
No checked figure yet. CBS (Statistics Netherlands) and Nuffic have current figures. Please check before relying on any number.

Germany bachelor's tuition per year: 0 to 3000 EUR. Most public universities charge no tuition to international students, only a semester contribution (about €150 to 350). Baden-Württemberg has charged non-EU students about €1,500 a semester (check). Private universities charge €5,000 to 20,000 or more.
Germany master's tuition per year: 0 to 3000 EUR. Same as undergraduate. Many English-taught master's programmes are listed in the DAAD database.
Germany living cost per year: 11904 to 14500 EUR. The blocked account amount for the student visa is €11,904 a year (€992 a month) in 2026. Big cities cost more.

Graduates of German universities can stay up to 18 months to look for a job in their field, and can work any job during that time. The EU Blue Card needs a job paying at least €50,700 a year in 2026 (€45,934.20 for shortage occupations and recent graduates).
Typical graduate starting pay is about €45,000 to 56,000 a year (secondary estimate). Check Destatis.
China bachelor's tuition per year: 14000 to 50000 CNY. Bachelor's tuition at one university on the CSC page is about ¥13,800 to 14,600 a year. Other guides give wider ranges.
China master's tuition per year: 15000 to 72000 CNY. Master's tuition from about ¥15,400 at some universities to ¥72,000 in guides.
China living cost per year: 24000 to 60000 CNY. Roughly ¥2,000 to 5,000 a month depending on the city. The CSC stipend (¥2,500 to 3,500 a month) is a rough benchmark.
Staying to work usually needs a job offer and a work permit. Settling in China is uncommon for foreign graduates.
Not covered. Pay depends heavily on the city and the employer.

Singapore bachelor's tuition per year: 21400 to 39700 SGD. NUS 2026/27 reports: about S$21,400 to 22,200 with the MOE Tuition Grant, about S$33,400 to 39,700 without it. Medicine about S$87,800 with the grant.
Singapore master's tuition per year: 15000 to 45000 SGD. Varies by university and programme.
Singapore living cost per year: 12000 to 24000 SGD. Roughly S$1,000 to 2,000 a month. Housing is the largest cost.

Graduates need an Employment Pass to work. In 2026 the minimum qualifying salary is S$5,600 a month for most sectors (S$6,200 in financial services), rising to S$6,000 and S$6,600 from 1 January 2027. Candidates must also pass the COMPASS points test.

Fresh graduates from the local universities had a median gross monthly salary of S$4,500 in 2025 (NUS S$4,746, NTU S$4,550, SMU S$4,747). NUS Computing graduates earned a median of S$6,400. Note: the local graduate median (S$4,500) is below the Employment Pass minimum (S$5,600), so a foreign graduate needs a better-than-median offer to stay.
